Ambuj Nath, J:

Petitioner-Rameshwar Mahto has filed this revision application against the judgment dated 03.09.2008, passed by Shri Goutam Mahapatra, Additional Judicial Commissioner-I, Khunti in Criminal Appeal No. 74/2006, whereby and wherein, the learned Additional Judicial Commissioner-I, Khunti partly allowed the appeal of the petitionerl by modifying the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 24.02.2006, passed by Shri Rajendra Bahadur Pal, Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Khunti in Case No. C 33/1999, holding the petitioner guilty of the offences under sections 498A I.P.C and section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act and thereby sentencing him to undergo R.I for three years along with a fine of Rs. 100/- for the offence under section 498A I.P.C and R.I for six months along with a fine of Rs. 100/- for the offence under section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
In default of payment of fine, he was further directed to undergo S.I for one month.
All the sentences were ordered to run concurrently.
Learned Appellate Court acquitted the petitioner of the charge under section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The sentence under section 498A of I.P.C. was also reduced to period of six months with fine of Rs. 100.

sentences.text: Prosecution case was instituted on the basis of the complaint filed by the complainant / opposite party no. 2-Shailo Devi, alleging therein that she was married to the petitioner on 03.06.1996.
After marriage, she was residing at the matrimonial home.
After marriage, petitioner started demanding a motorcycle and Rs. 5,000/- in dowry.
To enforce the demand, she was tortured and ultimately, she was driven away from the matrimonial home.
3. In order to prove its case, complainant / opposite party no. 2 has adduced both oral and documentary evidence.
Petitioner has also adduced oral evidence in his defence.
Both the learned Trial Court as well as the learned Appellate Court have come to a concurrent findings regarding the guilt of the petitioner.
4. Opposite party no. 2-Shailo Devi has been examined as C.W-4.
She has supported the allegation made out in her complaint.
She has stated that she was married to the petitioner on 03.06.1996.
After marriage, petitioner started demanding a motorcycle.
On 05.06.1996, she was driven away from the matrimonial home.
She has also stated that she had no issue from the wedlock.
She has further stated that on 16.06.1999, she went to the matrimonial home with her father and brother and the matter was pacified.
She again started residing there.
On 20.06.1999, her husband tried to strangulate her and snatched all her jewelleries and again she was driven away from the matrimonial home.
In her cross-examination, she has stated that she had gone to her matrimonial home on 16.06.1999 but she was finally driven away from the matrimonial home on 20.06.1999.
3. Lil Mohan (C.W-1), Yogendra Mahto (C.W-2), Ramphal Mahto (C.W- 3) and Bhim Mahto (C.W-5), all have supported the case of the complainant.
They have stated that the complainant was married to the petitioner.
After marriage, petitioner was demanding a motorcycle and to enforce the demand, she was tortured and ultimately, she was driven away from the matrimonial home
. These witnesses have stated the precise date when the demand was made by the petitioner.
They have also stated the date on which the opposite party no. 2 was driven away from the matrimonial home.
From perusal of the statement of Guhia Mahto (D.W-1), it transpires that he is the uncle of the petitioner.
He has stated that the opposite party no. 2 had come to her matrimonial home only once and thereafter, she did not return.
He has stated that he had gone to bring her back to the matrimonial home, but he cannot stay the date on which he had gone to the house of the father of the opposite party no. 2.
He has denied the suggestion that the petitioner was demanding Rs. 5,000/- and a motorcycle from the opposite party no. 2.
His evidence does not inspire much confidence.

4. From the aforesaid facts, it is apparent that the opposite party no. 2 and her witnesses have corroborated each other on the point that the petitioner was demanding a motorcycle as dowry and to enforce the demand, she was tortured and ultimately, she was driven away from the matrimonial home.
Complainant and her witnesses have stated the specific date on which such demand was made and when she was driven away from her matrimonial home.

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid facts, I am of the opinion that the opposite party no. 2 has been able to prove her case against the petitioner beyond all reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, judgment of conviction, so modified by the learned Appellate Court, holding the petitioner guilty of the offence under section 498A I.P.C, is affirmed.
6. The occurrence has taken place in the year 1999.
Learned Appellate Court has reduced the quantum of sentence under section 498A I.P.C to the period of R.I for six months along with a fine of Rs. 100/-.
The modified sentence passed by the learned Appellate Court is accordingly upheld.
7. This revision application is dismissed.
Pending I.A, if any, stands disposed of.

(Ambuj Nath, J) In the High Court of Jharkhand, Ranchi Dated 16th September 2023 Ranjeet/
